title: Four Public Trust Infrastructures — Money, Knowledge, Science and Humanitarian Access
status: E2 strong structural synthesis with E3 research questions
purpose: Crystallize the first cross-domain use of the entity dossier system by comparing four institutions whose outputs depend on sustained public/stakeholder trust but whose trust objects differ.
central_insight: Trust is not merely reputation. In all four cases, durable trust depends on alignment among a legitimate purpose (Spirit), competent sensing/decision/coordination (Mind), sufficient material capacity (Body), controlled access (Door), observability/accountability (Eye) and outcomes (Fruit).

trust_objects.trust_object: free knowledge infrastructure, privacy and continuity of access
shared scientific infrastructure and long-horizon collective inquiry
neutral humanitarian access, protection and assistance

common_mechanism.question: What mandate makes the institution worth trusting?
How does it know, decide, correct and coordinate?
What resources and infrastructure make the promise executable?
Who can enter, act, access or block the system?
What can outsiders/participants observe, audit or challenge?
What outcomes justify continuation of the trust relationship?
Which consequences or populations remain hard to observe?

revelation: The project can compare institutions without comparing their missions directly. The comparable object is the architecture by which a mission becomes credible action.
mission_drift_hypothesis: A useful early-warning pattern is cross-layer divergence: Spirit stays stable in public language while Mind optimizes different metrics or Body reallocates resources toward different ends. This is a research hypothesis requiring longitudinal entity evidence.
goodhart_guard: Fruit must remain multi-dimensional; if one trust metric becomes the target, it can become detached from the underlying trust object.
door_guard: The same infrastructure that creates trusted access can create chokepoint power. Dossiers should therefore record alternative routes, appeal mechanisms and who controls admission.
concrete_next_tests: For each entity, build a 10-year timeline of mission language, resource allocation, governance changes and major outcome metrics.
Identify one Door whose rules changed and test effects on access/capability.
Identify one Shadow/missingness mechanism that materially changes interpretation.
Compare public purpose with budget/resource distribution without presuming drift.
Record at least one case where correction/revision visibly changed policy or practice.
